newsitem.title: USA: First American helicopter museum opens.
newsitem.headline: First American helicopter museum opens.

text.p: More than half a century after helicopters first took to the air, America's first museum dedicated to the improbable flying machines opens this weekend outside Philadelphia.

The American Helicopter Museum and Education Centre, housed in a former helicopter manufacturing plant, aims to showcase historically significant helicopters and educate the public about their role in military and civilian life.

"This is an institution that will preserve a very important part of history," Igor Sikorski Jr., son of the builder of the first successful helicopter, said at opening ceremony of the museum on Friday.
"My interest has been in preserving aviation history. What's interesting to me is how much we have lost of it," Sikorski said.
The museum officially opens to the public on Saturday.
Highlights of the museum include three pioneering helicopters on long-term loan from the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum in Washington.

They are the Piasecki PV-2, which in 1943 became the second helicopter to fly in the United States; the only prototype of the Sikorski XR-4, the world's first production helicopter; and the earliest surviving Bell helicopter, the Bell model 30 -- the inspiration for modern police helicopters.

Other aircraft among the 12 now on display at the museum are a Bell H-13, made famous as a Korean War rescue helicopter delivering injured soldiers on outboard stretchers to M.A.S.H. field hospitals, and a version of the Vietnam War workhorse, the Bell UH-1 "Huey."
The world's first successful helicopter, the Sikorski VS 300, whose first free flight was in May, 1940, is at the Henry Ford Museum in Michigan.
